We ran identical campaigns across 5 platforms. The results challenged everything we assumed about B2B paid media.

Same offer. Same audience. Same budget. Same creative concept.

→ Reddit: $4.20 CPL (lowest cost, highest engagement)
→ TikTok: $6.10 CPL (yes, for B2B)
→ Meta: $8.30 CPL (best for creative testing)
→ Google: $11.50 CPL (most predictable)
→ LinkedIn: $38.00 CPL (2.5x better pipeline conversion)

The takeaway isn't that one platform wins. It's that platform mix > platform choice.

Most teams only run 2 platforms. Not because the others wouldn't work — but because each one means another dashboard, another reporting format, another learning curve.

Synter's AI Agents manage all 5 from one interface. Same creation flow. Unified reporting. The strategic decision stays with you. The execution across platforms is handled.

Run your own cross-platform test → syntermedia.ai

→ Conversion tracking auto-configured (GTM tag + conversion action + container published)

Manual equivalent: 45 minutes of clicking through Google Ads UI, plus another 20 for tracking setup.

This is what the Campaign IDE changes. Not the strategy — that's still hers. The 47 clicks between decision and execution.

Try Synter's Campaign IDE → syntermedia.ai

posts.linkedin_text:
We charge $49/month. Whether you manage $5K or $500K in ad spend.

Every advisor told us to charge percentage of ad spend. "That's how the industry works."

But percentage-of-spend pricing has a structural problem: the tool makes more money when you spend more, not when you get better results.

A tool that finds $10K/month in wasted spend is financially penalized for telling you about it.

Flat pricing at $49/month means:
→ We're incentivized to help you find waste and cut it
→ We win when you stay, not when you spend more
→ Same full platform whether you're a solo buyer or a 20-person agency
→ No surprise bills when a client increases budget

This isn't a promotional price or a loss leader. This is how we believe ad tools should be priced.

Aligned incentives > maximum extraction.

6 months in, this is the decision we feel best about.

Get started → syntermedia.ai/get-started

Synter now has the most comprehensive MCP server in advertising. Here's why that matters more than any feature we've shipped.

MCP (Model Context Protocol) lets AI agents like Claude, Cursor, and Amp execute actions through external tools.

When someone asks an AI agent to "create a Google Ads campaign" or "pull my Meta performance data," the agent routes to whichever MCP server can handle it.

The user never compares alternatives. The agent picks the tool.

Synter's MCP server supports:
→ 100+ executable actions
→ 10+ ad platforms (Google, Meta, LinkedIn, Reddit, TikTok, Microsoft, X, Amazon DSP, Trade Desk, StackAdapt)
→ Full campaign lifecycle: research → create → launch → optimize → report
→ Creative generation with Imagen 4
→ CRM audience sync across all platforms
→ Automatic OAuth injection and audit logging

For developers building marketing automation: connect your agent to Synter's MCP server and your tool can manage ads across every major platform.

For agencies: the tools your team uses will increasingly be selected by AI agents, not by humans browsing G2.

Being the default MCP server for advertising is the new being #1 on Google.

Documentation → syntermedia.ai/developer
